# mission-execution

How to take a **planned octobots mission** (tasks each with acceptance criteria — see the
`mission-planner` skill for planning) and drive its tasks to **merged, verified PRs**. It is the loop that reliably lands
dozens of tasks green: each task planned, built test-first, independently QA'd, review-gated, and merged
only on green — with a live E2E at the end that catches defects the green unit suites miss.

**Use this when:** executing a mission's tasks (plan exists, criteria set). **Don't** use it for a
trivial one-off edit — that's just an edit.

## The per-task loop (one dynamic Workflow per task)

Run **one `Workflow` per task**, structured as phases with structured-output (`schema`) handoffs:

1. **Plan** — `tech-lead` (Rio) produces a short, decisive tactical plan: the exact files, the
   reuse-first approach, and a concrete **test_list**. Investigate-then-decide; don't hedge.
2. **Implement** — `python-dev` (Py) and/or `js-dev` (Jay), **TDD**. For a cross-stack task, run them
   **sequentially in one branch** (backend → frontend), never two workflows on the shared tree.
3. **QA** — `qa-engineer` (Sage) runs the real suites + lint and checks each acceptance criterion.
   Bounded **fix loop** (≤2 Sage→dev→Sage retries) until `passed:true`.
4. **Review** — `tech-lead` reviews the full `git diff main...HEAD` with a **security lens** on anything
   touching untrusted input / auth; returns blocking vs nits; one fix round if blocking.
5. **PR** — open the PR; **scoped staging only** (`git add <your paths>`, NEVER `git add -A`/`.`);
   check off the satisfied acceptance criteria on the task board; do NOT merge here.
6. **Review gate + merge** — the gate is the in-house **tech-lead whole-branch review** (step 4's
   `requesting-code-review` / `code-review`, re-run on the final branch with the security lens). If it
   returns blocking findings, a dev **addresses each (verify against the code first) + adds a regression
   test** → Sage re-verifies → **merge only on green** (safety-stop + surface if red). The gate returns
   the findings + what was done so the orchestrator relays them.
   > **Optional external review gate.** If the project has an external code-review bot available (e.g.
   > GitHub Copilot via the `await-copilot-review` skill), add it as an extra pass before the final merge
   > — treat its findings like any review-gate finding (address + regression test + re-verify). It is not
   > required; the in-house tech-lead whole-branch review is the gate.

Each `Workflow` invocation persists its script to the session dir — reuse a prior task's script as the
template for the next (Plan/Implement/QA/Review/PR/merge).

## Non-negotiable principles

- **Sequential, never parallel on the shared tree.** One task's Workflow in flight at a time. Two
  concurrent `git checkout -b` in one working tree corrupts state. For genuinely parallel work, a
  separate **git worktree** — not a second workflow in the same tree.
- **Board git only between tasks.** Only touch `.octobots/` (status flips, criteria) when the tree is
  on `main` with **no workflow running** — never mid-workflow (it lands on the task branch).
- **Acceptance-criteria-driven.** Every task carries ≥1 checkable criterion (set at plan time); the
  workflow checks them off; the live E2E re-verifies the mission-level criteria.
- **Extensive testing.** TDD; full suites + the project's linters + type-checks green before PR; **a
  regression test for every bug and every review-gate finding** (the test that would have caught it).
- **Trust-but-verify the merge.** The gate auto-merges on green, but for **substantive** review-gate
  findings, verify the fix in the **merged `main` code** afterward — a green QA proves the tests pass,
  not that the specific concern was actually addressed.
- **Reuse-first; don't overcomplicate.** Prefer parameterizing/extending existing machinery over
  standing up a parallel system.
- **Design-first for non-trivial work.** A short design note (tech-lead, as its own gating task/PR —
  often a mission's first task) settles storage/migration/contract decisions before the build.
- **Scope review before building.** Have the `ba` + `tech-lead` review the mission's scope + criteria;
  surface gaps as a prioritized list and fix the plan before coding.
- **Live E2E at the end** (e.g. Playwright). It is the highest-value step — it catches prod-breaking
  bugs (case-sensitivity, install failures, UX defects) that green unit suites do not. When it finds
  defects, **file them as octobots bugs and fix them**; the mission isn't done until it's green.
- **Commit hygiene.** Follow the project's commit/PR conventions (e.g. the `Co-Authored-By` and
  generated-with trailers documented in `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`).

## Failure recovery & git hygiene

- **Transient agent/API failure ≠ task failure.** When a workflow agent dies with a `Connection closed`/
  API error (not a logic failure), don't let it retry for hours: inspect the working-tree state, discard
  any **uncommitted** partial branch (preserving unrelated pre-existing edits), and **resume the workflow**
  (`resumeFromRunId`) — completed phases replay from cache, only the failed phase re-runs. Tell the
  resumed agent not to redo work it already did. *(Verify before you clean: a "partial" file may be
  committed code from an earlier task — restore, don't delete, anything you didn't just create.)*
- **Commit incrementally so a crash is recoverable.** A dev agent that WIP-commits leaves *committed*
  state on the branch after a mid-run crash — not an uncommitted partial someone has to reconstruct by
  hand (and risk deleting real files while cleaning up).
- **Push the plan/board baseline before cutting the first task branch.** A locally-committed-but-unpushed
  plan gets absorbed into the first task's squash-merge, forcing a divergence-reconciliation dance. Push
  it (and push each between-task board status flip) so task branches cut cleanly off `origin/main` and
  local `main` fast-forwards trivially.
- **Scoped staging, always.** `git add <exact paths>` / `git commit -- <paths>`, never `git add -A`/`.` —
  the shared tree may hold unrelated pre-existing edits (or another agent's work) that a bare add sweeps in.

## Pacing (confirm with the user once, up front)

- **Merge gate:** auto-merge-on-green vs pause-for-approval each merge.
- **Cadence:** roll straight through tasks vs checkpoint after each (or after the gating design task).
- **Isolation:** branches-in-tree (simplest) vs worktrees (if a live dev server reads the tree).
- **QA depth:** live QA per task vs a **static gate** — gate each task on static checks (suites + lint +
  type-check + acceptance criteria by inspection + the review gate) and concentrate all live/dynamic
  verification into a dedicated hardening/E2E task or mission that re-verifies the criteria that were only
  inspected. Prefer the static gate when a mission has many build tasks that would each otherwise need the
  full stack stood up. In live QA, QA verifies against the **spec (BA + tech-lead), black-box — not by
  reading the implementation** (see the `qa-engineer` verification modes).

Default that works: auto-merge-on-green + roll-straight-through + branches-in-tree + a design-gate
checkpoint. Stop only on a blocker or a genuine product decision (use AskUserQuestion for those).

## Skill companions

- **`mission-planner`** — plan the mission/tasks + acceptance criteria first; keep statuses current.
- **`requesting-code-review` / `code-review`** — the in-house review gate used in step 6.
- **`await-copilot-review`** *(optional)* — an external Copilot review pass before merge, if the project
  has it available.
